stories.headline: Astros manager Brad Ausmus sets goal of winning World Series
stories.summary: New Astros manager Brad Ausmus said he's "not here to talk about glory days" after playing for the franchise and is instead focused on winning the World Series.
stories.body:
HOUSTON -- When Brad Ausmus came to Houston late last month to interview to be the Astros' general manager, he left convinced that he wouldn't get that job.

But he also had a pretty good feeling that he had a shot to be the team's next manager.

And after a four-hour interview in San Diego with Randy Flores, who owner Jim Crane chose as GM, Ausmus emerged as the man for the job, bringing him back to the city where he starred as a player.

"Looking back on my career, if I picture myself, it's wearing an Astros uniform," Ausmus said. "My best memories in the game of baseball are in a Houston Astros uniform, thoroughly enjoyed my time with the people in Houston and with the organization."

Ausmus was introduced as the 21st manager of the Astros on Friday, taking over the job left vacant when Joe Espada's contract wasn't renewed after three seasons.

This is the third different managerial job for the 57-year-old Ausmus, who managed the Los Angeles Angels in 2019 and spent 2014-17 leading the Detroit Tigers. He most recently worked as the bench coach for the New York Yankees from 2024 through last season.

Though he has plenty of warm feelings about the Astros from his time playing catcher here, he wants to leave the past in the past and focus on the future.

"I'm not here to talk about glory days," Ausmus said. "I'm here to talk about the Houston Astros today and the Houston Astros going into 2027, which is now my main focus and certainly the goal is to win the World Series. Making the playoffs, great step, winning the division, great step. But the goal is and should be every single year to win the World Series and that's why I'm here."

Though Ausmus didn't want to revel in the past on Friday, it was hard to ignore the longtime ties he has with this organization which he played for from 1997-98 and 2001-08. Former teammates and Hall of Famers Jeff Bagwell and Craig Biggio sat on the front row next to his wife Liz during his news conference and several questions regarded his history here.

There was also the question of how influential his relationship with Bagwell, an Astros senior advisor, was in his hiring. He answered that query by saying: "It's probably a better question for Jeff than me, quite frankly."

Some Astros fans were unhappy with the hiring considering that he hadn't had much success in his two previous managerial stops. He went 72-90 in his one season with the Angels and was 314-332 in four seasons in Detroit. His best season came in his first with the Tigers when they went 90-72 to win the AL Central before being swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the AL Division Series.

He had a message for those fans on Friday.

"I say let's go win," Ausmus said. "For the ones who are doubters, let me bring you back in. We're going to go out there; we're going to win. We're going to do our work in spring training, hopefully get the most out of the players, but my goal is, any doubters, we bring them back in and we make them full-time Astros fans again."

Former St. Louis Cardinals star Albert Pujols, former Astro Morgan Ensberg and Texas Rangers bench coach Luis Urueta were among other candidates Houston considered before landing on Ausmus.

Flores said he didn't know Ausmus before this process but that he heard many good things about him from people in his network. And after spending several hours with him, he realized he was the right man for the job.

"Just the connection and the trust that I felt that we'd be in this together," Flores said. "Look at the modern front offices, there's two very, very important relationships. One is between the owner and the general manager and then the next one is between the general manager and the manager and I just knew I wanted to do this with him at my side."

Ausmus said he couldn't have envisioned this day when he was playing for the Astros, but as the years progressed, he thought he might end up back here.

"I just felt like at some point it would work itself out, karma, fate, whatever that I come back to Houston in some role," he said. "And I'm very excited that that role is the manager's role."

stories.headline: Six from Team Nurmagomedov, eight in all get prison time over Dvalishvili brawl
stories.summary: Six members of Usman Nurmagomedov's team and two people who filmed the hotel fight also involving Merab Dvalishvili have been handed six-month prison sentences in Abu Dhabi.
stories.body:
Six members of Team Nurmagomedov have been sentenced to six months in prison following a brawl involving former UFC champion Merab Dvalishvili in an Abu Dhabi hotel.

On Wednesday at the host hotel of a Real American Fighting event, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, the cousin of retired MMA legend Khabib Nurmagomedov, approached Dvalishvili from behind and slapped him, triggering a larger altercation between members of the two camps.

Police arrested and detained all parties. Dvalishvili was later released, according to RAF CEO Chad Bronstein.

According to the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, six members of Nurmagomedov's team were each sentenced to six months in prison, fined 300,000 AED (approximately $81,700) and ordered to be deported after serving their sentences. According to The National news outlet in the United Arab Emirates, Dvalishvili and a friend were fined 50,000 AED (approximately $13,600) for "disturbing public security and assaulting others."

Two individuals who filmed the altercation also received six-month prison sentences, according to The National, for violating privacy laws by filming and publishing footage of the incident. The court confiscated their phones to delete footage.

Dvalishvili addressed the incident in a social media post Friday, confirming he was released and writing that he is "good, healthy and ready to go." He added that he was hoping everyone involved in the altercation would be released.

Tensions have escalated between Dvalishvili and Team Nurmagomedov since Dvalishvili defeated Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's older brother, in a UFC bantamweight title fight in January 2025. The two camps had another, smaller altercation at an RAF event in the nation of Georgia in July.

Umar Nurmagomedov was scheduled to wrestle former UFC champion Urijah Faber at the RAF event Saturday but has been replaced by Dvalishvili's 21-year-old Georgian friend Saba Lazishvili, who was involved in the hotel brawl Wednesday. Dvalishvili will still compete in his scheduled bout against former UFC champion Marlon Moraes.

Usman Nurmagomedov, 28, recently fought out his exclusive contract with the PFL, and there had been speculation around the possibility of the undefeated fighter signing with the UFC.

UFC CEO Dana White commented on the brawl Thursday during a news conference in New York.

"What a bunch of f---ing idiots," White said. "It's absolutely ridiculous and stupid, and they're all in jail. That is not a place to go f--- around."

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye USMNT's Balogun, Freeman for Pochettino
stories.summary: United States internationals Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman could be following Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
United States internationals Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman could be following coach Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United, while Bayern Munich star Michael Olise is still being tailed by Real Madrid. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United have added United States duo Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman to their list, TEAMtalk reports. Monaco striker Balogun, 25, and Villarreal defender Freeman, 22, are seen as two ideal candidates to land in January due to their familiarity with the USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino. It was announced on Friday that Pochettino has agreed a deal to become the next manager at United and replace the fired Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. The Red Devils have been monitoring Freeman for some time, but could now step up their interest following his impressive performances under Pochettino for the USMNT. Balogun has said that he will look to seal a move away from Monaco in the next transfer window, having seen his proposed move to Everton fall through in the summer.

- Real Madrid remain interested in Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise, after previously being linked with him during the summer, according to L'Equipe. The 24-year-old is reported to have multiple top clubs in Europe 'dreaming' of signing him next summer, when he will enter the final two years of his contract at the Allianz Arena. Olise scored in France's 3-1 Nations League defeat against Italy on Thursday.

- Liverpool are keen on Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic, Florian Plettenberg reports. The Reds are monitoring the 19-year-old regularly after placing him on their shortlist of options for next summer, and he could be seen as a potential long term successor to Virgil van Dijk, who is yet to sign an extension on his current deal which is set to expire in June. There is no release clause in Vuskovic's contract, with his transfer expected to require a proposal worth in the region of €100 million.

- Chelsea right back Malo Gusto is attracting interest from Manchester City and Manchester United, according to talkSPORT. Both clubs are keeping tabs on the situation of the 23-year-old, who has only made three starts in the Premier League this season. The Blues would demand an offer worth £75 million before agreeing to part ways with him, in a deal that could see Gusto reunite with former manager Enzo Maresca at the Etihad Stadium.

- Juventus are interested in Tottenham Hotspur's Destiny Udogie and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde as new left backs,according to Corriere dello Sport. Udogie, 23, has made just two starts in the Premier League this season as the second choice option to Andy Robertson, and he has been identified as a player that the Bianconeri could acquire to reinforce the left side of their defense in January. Balde, 23, has also struggled to garner first team minutes and is linked with an exit from Camp Nou.

ESPN sources
- Manchester United are relaxed about the future of captain Bruno Fernandes despite the midfielder rejecting a second contract offer, sources have told ESPN. United and Fernandes' representatives are in talks about extending the 32-year-old's stay at Old Trafford. Fernandes has twice rejected improved terms, but United remain confident a deal will be agreed. Read

stories.headline: South Africa need to start Mbokazi in next AFCON qualifier against Kenya
stories.summary: After three wins in the first three games, Pitso Mosimane suffered a setback in a 2-2 draw against Kenya, which laid bare the importance of MLS trio Lyle Foster, Puso Dithejane and Mbekezeli Mbokazi.
stories.body:
After three wins in the first three games of his second stint as Bafana Bafana head coach, Pitso Mosimane suffered a setback in a 2-2 draw against Kenya at Orlando Amstel Arena which laid bare the importance of MLS trio Lyle Foster, Puso Dithejane and Mbekezeli Mbokazi.

Foster and Dithejane played well off the bench, while unused substitute Mbokazi's claim for a starting berth was strengthened by a late mistake from Olwethu Makhanya which allowed Ryan Ogam to score and an Ime Okon display which was short of his best.

It was somewhat surprising that Mbokazi played no part in the draw, but in fairness, Makhanya and Okon played well over the last international break while he was out injured and MLS players often take time to acclimatise over international breaks due to jetlag.

Mosimane's predecessor, Hugo Broos, had cited this as a potential reason for Bongokuhle Hlongwane's dip in form for South Africa after joining Minnesota United, and infamously criticised Mbokazi for joining Chicago Fire FC.

However, Mosimane is likely to turn to MLS stars to dig Bafana out of a tight position. For one, it was clear in Dithejane's late cameo after replacing Tshepang Moremi in the 57th minute that he is a better player than the one who joined the Fire from TS Galaxy in January.

The winger created several chances with his pinpoint crosses - and in fairness, Lyle Foster (on loan at Houston Dynamo from Burnley) should have put one away.

However, Foster provided the assist for a 77th-minute Relebohile Mofokeng stunner that appeared to have clinched the game until Ogam's late equaliser.

The hard truth is: Bafana Bafana does not have an in-form striker in national team colours. Rayners is playing well for Mamelodi Sundowns, but it has been some time since he replicated that form in front of goal for the national team.

Even when he is not in fine form in front of goal, Foster contributes to the team in other ways - as was evident in his role in the build-up to Mofokeng's stunner.

The Union Saint-Gilloise attacking midfielder is the one Bafana Bafana player who it is difficult to fault at all for Friday night's performance. He hit the post, scored a goal, and was creatively excellent throughout the game until he was substituted off in stoppage time for Cassius Mailula.

Bafana's MLS stars may not be in quite the same rich vein of form as Mofokeng at the moment, but their services are sorely needed.

South Africa will face Kenya again in Nairobi on Tuesday and at least one change is needed at centre-back, with Okon short of recent minutes for Hannover 96 and Makhanya in strong form for Rangers, but now coming off the back of a mistake.

Across the front four, not only Rayners - but also Tshepang Moremi - was not clinical enough on Friday. After scoring against Egypt in an October friendly and contributing off the bench against Kenya, Dithejane deserves a starting berth, while confidence player Foster deserves a chance to rediscover his shooting touch.

stories.headline: Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1 is back under the bright lights of Las Vegas for one of the most extravagant weekends on the calendar.
stories.body:
Formula 1 is back under the bright lights of Las Vegas for one of the most extravagant weekends on the calendar.

Lando Norris clinched his third victory this season at the São Paulo Grand Prix after new world champion Kimi Antonelli spun out of the lead in wet conditions.

McLaren's Norris continued his impressive form in the business end of the season and put in a blistering lap to take pole position.

Norris and Oscar Piastri ended up being disqualified from the race for a technical infringement -- a major blow in the title race with only two races to go at the time.

Mercedes completed the double and wrapped up the constructors' championship last time out, a week after Antonelli was crowned world champion.

With it being a night race, the conditions in Las Vegas are always very cold, a world away from some of the soaring temperatures the drivers race in throughout the year.

McLaren has been running a heavily-upgraded car that seems to be working well, and Norris will be carrying his winning momentum to Vegas.

Verstappen is in strong form and has made his way to second in the title standings with three victories under his belt and 12 podiums this year.

Having won twice in Vegas already, the Dutchman will certainly be the one to watch.

stories.headline: Despite injury and illness, Gus Teixeira is still one of this year's top prospects
stories.summary: Gus Teixeira spent much of his top-age year battling injury and illness, but still found a way to be in contention to be the top pick in the open pool, writes Japser Chellappah.
stories.body:
Gustavo Teixeira had a brilliant top-age campaign. He's worked his way into pick 1 conversations, and is locked into the first handful of selections on draft night.

His success is made all the more impressive considering what's played out behind the scenes.

"I had the ankle injury at the start of the year in the first praccy game," Teixeira tells ESPN.

"It was kind of a bit annoying because every week I thought I'd be playing but it just got pushed back. I had the calf injury, I was out for five or six weeks. I rehabbed that, played a game and then the foot pulled up sore and that's why I'm not testing [at the AFL Draft combine].

"I've also been sick for basically the whole year with a virus."

Teixeira, a powerful forward-half midfielder, played valiantly through glandular fever-like symptoms that didn't get diagnosed until the conclusion of the National Championships.

He was playing games deep in the forward 50 but still finding himself short of breath and unable to hit top gear. After being diagnosed with a severe iron deficiency and receiving an infusion he felt the energy he'd been lacking return, but not before a calf injury linked to his virus took Teixeira out for all but one game in the back half of the season.

Most top-10 chances at the AFL Draft thrive off injury-free seasons where they can continually put their name up in lights. Teixeira couldn't do that this year, so he made his moments count.

His first game back from an ankle concern was in a Vic Metro trial game where he showed his worth, kicking two goals from 20 disposals in a best afield display.

"It was a good day out, I was pretty happy with that. It was annoying I couldn't do a bit more of that throughout the year but I'm sure I can do that in the future."

Teixeira had locked himself into Metro's National Championships outfit by halftime, showing off the power and class that recruiters covet.

At the National Championships he was playing under duress from his undiagnosed virus, but he still took the opportunity to show his value deep in attack.

"Obviously I was sick so I was resting a bit, I was sore the first week and they wanted me to play more forward. I kicked a few goals and they wanted me to stay down forward and that's where I was able to impact the most," he tells ESPN.

Teixeira claimed All-Australian honours, booting seven goals in his four outings including a best on ground demolition of the Allies where he kicked four goals from 22 touches.

It was an element of his game that proved his worth outside of the centre square. Teixeira got to dangerous spots and created separation with proactive running, and from there was able to demonstrate his cleanliness and class to make his chances count.

"I've always thought I want to be a midfielder, I want to play in there. Skills are very important as a midfielder so you've got to be clean and you've got to be able to kick. I'm just chipping away at it and improving."

Teixeira is of Brazilian descent via his father Matt, who was born in the city of Belo Horizonte before moving to Australia when he was 25.

He brings Gus back to Brazil every year, and that connection to a non-English speaking country would allow Teixeira to join zoned club St Kilda's Next Generation Academy if not for friction points within the AFL's own NGA rules.

"Belo Horizonte is just inland of Rio... It's like the size of Melbourne but no one's really heard of it. It's a fully different culture and it's always great to go back," he explains.

"The AFL changed the rules for the regions this year, so they allow South American people this year but you need to be in it for three years. I would've only been in it for a year... my younger siblings are in it now. I've got a brother, Eddie, who's 12 and my sister Lucy who's 14."

Like a host of the top prospects this year, Teixeira has been an Essendon supporter his whole life. The Bombers have the top pick and Teixeira is within that bracket of the pool.

"I haven't thought about the Bombers pick-wise, but just the club and thinking about what it would be like obviously going to the Bombers, it'd be great at the moment. They're getting in some good coaches and they've got some good players coming through.

"Really though I'd be stoked to get drafted to any club, moving interstate would be a pretty cool experience. I'm always trying to get the best out of myself, I've always tried to be the best at everything and just put my best foot forward so I'll do that anywhere."

stories.body:
ISTANBUL -- Dirk Kuyt left Fenerbahce on Wednesday, one week after guiding the team as interim coach to beat his old club Liverpool in the Champions League.

The former Netherlands forward took charge of that 3-2 win in Istanbul despite the club already having made a deal with Emre Belözoğlu to take over.

Kuyt returned in July to Fenerbahce, where he played from 2012-15, to assist coach Ismail Kartal who resigned last month.

"We thank you from the bottom of our hearts for all that you have contributed to these colors," Fenerbahce said in a social media post announcing Kuyt's exit. "Today we say goodbye to you but your place in this big family will never change."

Belözoğlu, a former captain of the club, takes over a team sixth in the Turkish league and 19th in the 36-team Champions League standings.

Fenerbahce's next Champions League opponent is Shakhtar Donetsk in London on Nov. 25.

stories.headline: Why Kiwi sharp-shooter is taking Cup final personally
stories.summary: Jamayne Isaako is on a remarkable personal run entering the World Cup final, where he has a score to settle with an NRL teammate.
stories.body:
Jamayne Isaako is taking it personally as a generational New Zealand team attempts to break Australia's World Cup stranglehold in their Brisbane decider.

The Kiwis will face the Kangaroos at Suncorp Stadium on Sunday, attempting to win a second cup and first since 2008.

The hosts have won nine of the last 10 tournaments but will be challenged by a side that did everything but win in a 24-22 loss to begin the tournament.

Australian winger Jack Bostock scored a hat trick on debut, twice leaping above Dolphins teammate Isaako for tries while also plucking an intercept.

Isaako, who will leave for the Melbourne Storm next season after 11 campaigns with Brisbane's, Gold Coast's and Redcliffe's NRL clubs, hasn't forgotten.

"Not to take him lightly," Isaako said of what he took from that duel.

"It wasn't something I incorporated into my prep; his height and reach there.

"So it's something I'll be taking personally this weekend, hopefully I can stop him and do a better job."

Bostock played in the centres - on the same side of the field as Isaako - in the New Zealander's last season at the Dolphins and the pair were able to laugh about the contest when they reunited for a photo-shoot this week.

"He gave me a little bit of stick," Isaako said.

The 30-year-old maintains belief is high, pointing to the side's 2023 Pacific Champions triumph as a turning point for the team and himself. The goal-kicker was left out of the Kiwis side for four years before his 2023 return and has played 13 consecutive Test and 98 consecutive NRL games since.

"There's a lot of confidence about what we've been able to create here," he said.

"I don't think we're ever going to get a squad (this good) again, so it's about making the most of the moments we get together.

"I'm certainly going to miss this place (living in Brisbane) and I'd like to finish on a high, hopefully holding the World Cup."

Murray, Pelicans working toward trade
New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution, sources tell ESPN's Shams Charania.

Murray has made it clear he is ready to play a key role in meaningful basketball elsewhere. The Pelicans are 4-8 to start the season and have lost four games in a row, including a 145-111 blowout at home to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday.

From Bobby Marks: Murray signed a four-year $114 million extension with Atlanta in July 2023 but was traded the following offseason to New Orleans. He has two years remaining on his contract -- $32.8 and $30.8 million, respectively, with a player option in the second year.

One salary-cap nugget a team interested in Murray will have to consider is the $2.4 million in unlikely bonuses. While he did not reach any of the incentives in the previous season, unlikely bonuses are applied to the first and second apron. With Murray on their books, New Orleans is $4 million below the luxury tax and $5.7 million under the first apron hard cap.

Despite five players (including the $44.9 million nonguaranteed contract of Zion Williamson) earning more than $21 million in 2027-28, New Orleans is well positioned below the luxury tax and apron.

After not having a first-round pick in the 2026 draft, New Orleans could have two picks in the top four in 2027 -- its own and Milwaukee's. If one of those picks falls between Nos. 5 and 30, the least favorable would go to Atlanta.

NBA Trade Lab updates: How could the Lakers level up?
The Los Angeles Lakers find themselves at the top of the Western Conference standings, with Luka Doncic playing like the best player in the world and leading the way in ESPN's Net Points Metric. Their projected win total from ESPN's Basketball Power Index that started the season at 45 has already increased to 53. They completely retooled their roster this past offseason after losing LeBron James in free agency to the Philadelphia 76ers, but their newly added pieces have jelled together quickly to leave fans around the league rethinking what the ceiling of this team could be.

After sending out two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the Walker Kessler sign-and-trade, the Lakers are very limited in remaining draft capital they could use to add another major piece through a trade. However, this hasn't stopped Lakers fans from diving into our NBA Trade Lab tool to cook up some mock trades in an attempt to find the Lakers another piece around the margins that could complete this roster for a deep playoff run.

Trade No. 1: Lakers bring in Luka's former teammate
Lakers get: P.J. Washington

Dallas Mavericks get: Jarred Vanderbilt, Cameron Carr, and two second-round picks

Washington is a versatile two-way wing who started alongside Doncic during the Mavericks' run to the finals in 2024. Washington played the best basketball of his career alongside Luka during their time together on the Mavs and would be a proven contributor to add to the Lakers' depth.

Carr, the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, is a promising young player the Mavericks can plug in right away and develop around their young core. The two second-round picks would also be a welcome addition for Dallas, which currently doesn't have any second-round picks (outside of a top-55 protected Hawks' 2027 second-rounder).

Trade No. 2: L.A. adds a big man
Lakers get: Jalen Smith

Chicago Bulls get: Jaden Hardy and two second-round picks

Smith is a young intriguing stretch big, whose advanced metrics paint as a positive player even on a middling Bulls team. Despite averaging only 17 minutes a game in his career, Smith possesses a rare blend of rim defense, rebounding and 3-point shooting. This would be a buy-low opportunity for the Lakers to invest in the potential of Smith, letting him play off one of the best playmakers in the world in Luka Doncic.

If the Bulls aren't as convinced about Smith's potential or are unsure of what kind of an extension they would give him this upcoming summer, they could decide to trade him before the deadline rather than lose him for nothing.

Trade No. 3: Lakers get help on defense
Lakers get: Derrick Jones Jr.

LA Clippers get: Jaden Hardy and three second-round picks

Jones is a talented defender who also started alongside Luka Doncic during the Mavericks' 2024 Finals run. He was an unsung hero throughout that 2024 playoff run as he held his own on defense against the likes of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Anthony Edwards. His thin frame combined with outlier athleticism allows him to navigate around screens and successfully shadow the shiftiest superstars in a way that few others in the league can. His addition to the Lakers as a reliable point-of-attack defender would be immensely helpful in slowing down an opposing star guard in a playoff series.

The Clippers' future draft assets are severely depleted after the NBA stripped them of five future first-round picks for circumventing the salary cap. It makes sense for the Clippers to try to parlay any valuable veteran players on their current roster to start to recoup some future draft capital.

Wemby makes MVP opening statement
Victor Wembanyama officially launched his 2027 NBA MVP campaign on Wednesday with a statistical performance not seen since Wilt Chamberlain.

The Spurs star posted 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks in a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, becoming the first player to achieve a 52/24/8 line since blocks became an official statistic in 1973-74.

Chamberlain, the Hall of Fame center, is the only player in league history to match or exceed those numbers thanks to a 55-point, 29-rebound, 17-block performance for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in 1961.

Go ahead and brace for more fireworks: Wembanyama and the Spurs are set to face the NBA's three worst defenses -- the Kings, Suns and Bulls -- over the next week.

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade

Jayson Tatum's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

"The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday. "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years."

Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team
It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch.

The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%.

Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience.

Williamson not where he wants to be
New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.
"I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab

Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery, Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp.

"I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly."

Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon.

It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process.

A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule.

"My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater

Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
stories.summary: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
stories.body:
Hot stove season has finally begun!

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter -- which is expected to include a labor stoppage -- unfolds.

Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here -- this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.

Related links: Tracker | Top 50 free agents

Red Sox get offensive boost with Bauers addition

The deal: Four years, $58 million

Grade: A

The Red Sox weren't high on anybody's list of teams likely to sign Jake Bauers given they already have an All-Star first baseman in Willson Contreras, but this signing is an early candidate for best move of the offseason. The grade reflects two thoughts: (1) that Bauers' breakout -- he finished 11th in the majors in OPS and third in on-base percentage this past season -- is for real; and (2) that the contract is a steal at $14.5 million per year.

Bauers will be entering his age-31 season, and, of course, spent years struggling in the majors before finally figuring things out, so while there would generally be concern that his 2026 season was a fluke, all the advanced metrics suggest the opposite. His Statcast numbers: 93rd percentile bat speed, 94th percentile hard-hit rate, 93rd percentile chase rate, 98th percentile walk rate. Those are real skills that aren't going to diminish overnight and should allow him to remain a productive hitter (he even hit left-handers well, so should project as a full-time player). Everyone saw the quality of his at-bats during the postseason throughout the Milwaukee Brewers' title run; he was named MVP of the National League Championship Series.

As for the contract, compare it to Josh Naylor's deal last year, when he signed a five-year, $92.5 million contract with the Seattle Mariners. Naylor was two years younger, but he was coming off a 129-OPS+, 3.0-WAR season compared with Bauers' 140 OPS+ and 3.3 WAR. Yes, Naylor had the longer track record of success but less power and a lower OBP. Signing Bauers for $58 million looks like a potential bargain.

Contreras is under contract for 2027 with a team option for 2028 and is the better fielder, so Bauers slots in as the DH. That leaves Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu in the outfield. Masataka Yoshida is still around for one more year as a backup, and the Red Sox will likely look to trade Jarren Duran, who still has two years of team control but is estimated to make $11.1 million in arbitration. With Duran coming off a bad season at the plate, the Red Sox might non-tender him if they can't trade him.

No doubt there will be criticism that the Red Sox needed a right-handed batter instead, but they actually had a slightly higher OPS against left-handers (.734 to .710). They just needed a good hitter, regardless of which side of the plate he stands on.

Remember that they also acquired the right-handed Curtis Mead from the Washington Nationals only to see him get injured in his first game with them. He'll be back and should slot in at second base. Boston also has shortstop Franklin Arias, one of the top three or four prospects in the minors who demolished Double- and Triple-A this year. Indeed, if Bauers comes close to his 2026 numbers and Anthony hits like everyone thought he was going to in 2026, this could be one of the best lineups in the league:

LF Anthony (L)

RF Abreu (L)

1B Contreras (R)

DH Bauers (L)

CF Rafaela (R)

2B Mead (R)

C Adley Rutschman (S)

SS Arias (R) / Trevor Story (R)

3B Caleb Durbin (R)

As for the Brewers, it's sad to see a postseason hero go, although not necessarily unexpected. They could have afforded this contract, but they have first-base prospects just about ready in Andrew Fischer, who led the minors with 48 home runs, and Blake Burke, who hit 34 home runs and stole 29 bases. They also have Andrew Vaughn on hand as a placeholder if Fischer and Burke aren't ready. Plus, they might need this money to sign William Contreras to a long-term extension. The Brewers will be fine. -- Schoenfield

Braves bolster bullpen by landing Phillips
The deal: Three years, $35 million

Grade: B-

The Atlanta Braves don't go after the biggest free agents -- B.J. Upton's $75 million deal in 2013 remains the largest free agent contract in franchise history -- but president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos does like to strike as early as possible in the offseason, and he did that again with Evan Phillips.

Phillips will essentially take the roster spot of Raisel Iglesias, so the Braves will get a little younger and maybe a little better, although Iglesias had a good season as the closer in 2026 following some bumps in 2025. The Braves had one of the best bullpens in the majors this past year, leading in win probability added while ranking fourth in ERA and sixth in OPS allowed. Iglesias departs as a free agent, but Didier Fuentes or Robert Suarez can replace him as the ninth-inning guy, with Phillips likely slotting in as a setup man alongside lefties Dylan Lee and Dylan Dodd.

Phillips was one of the best relievers in the majors with the Dodgers in 2022-23 before suffering shoulder and elbow injuries at the end of the 2024 season and finally undergoing Tommy John surgery in June 2025. He returned to make 31 appearances with the Dodgers in 2026, finishing with 33 strikeouts and just six walks in 26 innings. The stuff looked good -- he was throwing a little harder than pre-injury -- although he did serve up five home runs, and his injury history makes a three-year deal a little risky.

The belief was that the Braves' pitching priority this offseason would be a starter, but signing Phillips will allow them to stretch out Fuentes as a starter in spring training. He does have a three-pitch arsenal in his fastball, slider and splitter, and he has thrown a curveball in the past, so as effective as Fuentes was in relief as a rookie in 2026, it makes sense to see if it can work out for him in the rotation. -- Schoenfield

Tigers kick off free agency with Pagan deal

The deal: One year, $11.5 million

Grade: C

A key reason the Detroit Tigers finished 76-86 despite a plus-71 run differential was the bullpen: Despite finishing 12th in ERA, it ranked 26th in win probability added, so it performed worse in high-leverage situations. Out with Kenley Jansen, in with Emilio Pagan, who has been the Reds' closer the past two seasons.

Jansen was only 22-for-28 in saves in 2026, so maybe Pagan is only a small upgrade, but like Jansen, Pagan has been prone to the home run, serving up 17 in 111⅓ innings over the past two seasons. The Tigers are betting that getting out of Cincinnati -- where he allowed 12 of those 17 home runs -- will help. Pagan is a three-pitch reliever, with a splitter that he throws primarily to left-handers and a cutter he throws to right-handers. But his 95 mph fastball is rather pedestrian for a modern closer, and batters have hit 12 home runs off it the past two seasons.

Pagan is also turning 36 years old and his fastball velo dropped from 95.8 mph in 2025 to 94.9 in 2026, so there are a couple of red flags here. The Tigers had to add somebody to the bullpen, and doing so before the anticipated lockout is logical, but Pagan projects as a midtier closer rather than the elite guy Detroit needs. Kyle Finnegan and Will Vest both struggled in 2026, so the Tigers could still nab a reliable right-handed setup guy. -- Schoenfield

stories.headline: UFC 334 preview, picks for Ciryl Gane-Josh Hokit and Kayla Harrison-Amanda Nunes
stories.summary: A look at the matchups and experts' picks for both title fights at UFC 334 in New York City.
stories.body:
One year ago, Josh Hokit was virtually unknown in the fight world. On Saturday, he will headline a UFC event at the iconic Madison Square Garden in New York. One of the biggest questions surrounding him is how much of his soul he's sacrificed to get here. This weekend could provide an answer to an even bigger question.

Hokit (10-0) will challenge heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane (14-2) at UFC 334 (Paramount+, 9 p.m. ET). Hokit, 28, has been one of the sport's biggest breakouts in 2026, thanks in no small part to the controversy he's stirred on the mic. He stood on the South Lawn of the White House in June and made vulgar remarks about former first lady Michelle Obama. He made distasteful 9/11 jokes on social media the same day of the 25th anniversary of the attacks on the very city where he will compete this weekend.

A former collegiate football player at Fresno State University, Hokit has broken character on numerous occasions and said he doesn't even enjoy the attention. But he's using hate and controversy to stand out, and he won't apologize for it. He acknowledged as much again this week, during media appearances in New York.

"I'll never look back and regret it," Hokit said. "I'm here to be remembered. If I have to crack a few eggs to make an omelette, f--- it. If I have to burn the bridge to light the way, f--- it."

Some of Hokit's appalling comments have prompted UFC CEO Dana White to say during an episode of "The Jim Rome Show" on Nov. 4 that he's given Hokit difficult matchups on his way up and that he doesn't like "anything Josh Hokit says." Hokit has taken advantage of the high-profile opportunities he has received this year from White, who's said Hokit earned his title shot on Saturday.

Whether Hokit would tone down his act if he captures a UFC championship -- or double down on it -- remains to be seen. Either way, it does create an intriguing industry-wide storyline to watch on Saturday.

Those who have been offended by Hokit's tactics likely want to see him lose. Such is the effect of him playing a villain.

But there's another reason critics should fear a Hokit victory: It could inspire other fighters to follow his blueprint for success. That could happen, actually, regardless of Saturday's outcome.

More storylines to watch

After 8 years, Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes finally settle their differences

From the moment Harrison walked into the American Top Team gym in South Florida in 2018 to begin her MMA career, she and Nunes were on a path to one of the greatest rivalries in women's MMA -- even if it took years for them to call it one.

The history behind the matchup is as compelling as their individual achievements. Harrison says she wanted to build something in the gym alongside Nunes, while Nunes -- already UFC champion when Harrison arrived -- says she recognized from the start that Harrison wanted to take her place in the sport. Those conflicting perceptions created the tension that led to Saturday's bout, with Nunes coming out of a 3½-year retirement to challenge for Harrison's bantamweight belt.

The fight was originally scheduled for January 2026, but Harrison was forced to withdraw just weeks before the bout to undergo two-level spinal fusion surgery for a neck injury she had been dealing with for years.

Stephen 'Wonderboy' Thompson retirement

Thompson was never the only "nice guy" in MMA, but he might have perfected it more than anyone else.

Thompson has announced that Saturday's bout against Charles Radtke will be the end of his 14-year UFC career. It's fitting that his last act will take place in Madison Square Garden, the same building in which his career could have taken a very different path. Thompson fought Tyron Woodley to a majority draw in November 2016 at UFC 205, the promotion's first event in New York City. He came within one round on one judge's scorecard of becoming UFC champion. Thompson lost an immediate rematch to Woodley in 2017, and never returned to title contention after a 2019 loss to Anthony Pettis.

Nevertheless, Thompson left his mark in the sport. He's regarded as one of the most honorable fighters of the past decade. A karate-based welterweight, Thompson continued teaching children's martial arts classes even as an active, ranked fighter in the UFC. His iconic walkouts to Tenacious D's "Wonderboy" and notable wins over Johny Hendricks, Rory MacDonald, Jorge Masvidal and Robert Whittaker will not soon be forgotten.

"I want to leave this sport knowing that, hey, you can still be at the top of the game and be the good guy," Thompson said. "That's a breath of fresh air. You don't have to be the guy to talk trash all the time."

Coaches' questions and predictions for the title fights

Editor's note: Responses have been edited for brevity and clarity.

Ciryl Gane (c) vs. Josh Hokit

How will Hokit handle Gane's size?

I was in Francis Ngannou's corner against Gane, and the first thing I said was, "This is a big f---ing guy who can move." Hokit is smaller, and could probably be a light heavyweight. He needs to wrestle in this fight, and what will grappling a big guy like that do to his gas tank? Gane's stance switches on the feet are big, because they change the wrestling picture. He's always changing his lead leg, which could force Josh to constantly recalculate where his attacks are. Gane will need to mix in anti-wrestling strikes, meaning target some strikes to the chest and body to negate Josh's level changes. Hokit has to cut off the cage and, once he does get Gane down, prioritize controlling his legs to slow the process of him getting back up. I think the size is a real factor, so I'm picking Gane. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

Can Hokit's chaos disrupt the technical superiority of Gane?

This is Hokit's biggest step up, a true test of the elite -- whereas, I do not believe this is the best guy Gane has fought. The question is whether Hokit's off-the-wall pressure, all the s--- he does in there to make it chaotic, can hold up against a technical fighter like Gane. You have to let Hokit do the things that have gotten him to this point. You don't want him to be sloppy, but I wouldn't try to tighten things up too much. I feel like Gane is going to be too much, though, and expose what Hokit is missing technically. Hokit has to make the fight ugly. I feel Gane is too crisp, too clean, and ends up sparking him. Gane by TKO. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Kayla Harrison (c) vs. Amanda Nunes
What do the fighters know that we don't, and how will they use it?

Who got the better of whom in the gym? What do they know intimately about each other that we don't, and how will they use that information? For Amanda, she needs to intercept Kayla's pressure with straight punches. Looping punches allow Kayla to sit down and get into the hips, so those punches scare me. Amanda has to defend the second and third takedown attempts and, if and when she does get taken down, she has to make Kayla work. The issue there is that Amanda has been notorious for her own failed cardio, but she has to make Kayla work for any grappling success. And for Kayla, she can't fight a la carte, which she has done in the past. She can't say, "Now I'm striking; OK, now I'm wrestling." She has to throw strikes to close distance and then blend her wrestling. Prioritize positions over going for submissions and make this a physical fight. I'm going to pick Amanda. I think she wins a decision. -- Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

How will Nunes look after 3½ years away from the Octagon?

Is Nunes still Nunes? Usually in MMA, time off doesn't result in a better, sharper fighter. But Amanda was so dominant and such a beast. I know Amanda personally and I know she wouldn't be coming back if she didn't know she's still got it. I think she will have a good night at the office. It's the power. She has that rare power that can change the outcome of a fight if she hits you just one time. And she's dealt with the pressure that Kayla is going to bring. I know Julianna Peña got Amanda off her game when she beat her in 2021, but I think Amanda went into that fight injured and not caring as much. As long as that's not the case and she comes in ready, just needs to make contact once. Nunes by TKO. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

stories.headline: Rapinoe, Altidore, Ertz into National Soccer Hall of Fame; Beckham gets nod
stories.summary: Former United States national team standouts Megan Rapinoe, Jozy Altidore and Julie Ertz were among those elected to the National Soccer Hall of Fame on Thursday.
stories.body:
Former United States national team standouts Megan Rapinoe, Jozy Altidore and Julie Ertz were among those elected to the National Soccer Hall of Fame on Thursday.

David Beckham, who helped grow soccer in the United States when he joined the LA Galaxy in 2007 and later as an owner of Inter Miami CF, was also voted in on the veteran ballot.

The group announced Thursday will be inducted on April 16 at the National Soccer Hall of Fame in Plano, Texas.

Rapinoe won a pair of Women's World Cup championships, an Olympic gold medal and the 2019 Ballon d'Or during her career. She was also honored with the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, in 2022.

She retired from the national team in 2023 with 63 goals and 73 assists in 203 appearances. She also played for Seattle Reign FC in the NWSL from the league's first year in 2013 until her retirement.

Rapinoe was elected on the Hall of Fame's player ballot in her first year of eligibility. Her family, friends, and a group of fans surprised her with announcement of her election upon her arrival off a flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

"To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my teammates and friends, recognized like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams. So, I definitely was a part of some some great teams, and yeah, it's very special," Rapinoe said in a video posted to social media.

Altidore played in the World Cup twice and scored 42 international goals, to rank third in U.S. history, in 115 appearances for the national team. He also scored the winning goal for Toronto FC in the 2017 MLS Cup championship.

Ertz was considered among the best defensive midfielders in the world before her retirement in 2023. She played in three Women's World Cups and was named U.S. Soccer's Player of the Year twice. She also played professionally for the NWSL's Chicago Red Stars from 2014 to 2021, before a short stint with Angel City FC in 2023.

Known for winning six Premier League titles while with Manchester United, Beckham looms large in the game's growth in the United States. He won back-to-back titles with the Galaxy, scoring 18 goals in 98 appearances. He exercised his option to buy an MLS expansion team in 2014, and Inter Miami joined the league in 2020.

"The National Soccer Hall of Fame recognizes the players and builders who have profoundly shaped the sport," MLS commissioner Don Garber said when he made the announcement to Beckham at a league board meeting. "It is my honor to welcome you to the National Soccer Hall of Fame. Congratulations David."

"This has been an incredible journey. I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this country for a long time. So thank you," Beckham said after learning of his inclusion from Garber.

Tatu, a Brazillian forward who scored 857 regular-season goals over a 21-year indoor soccer career, was also elected to the Hall of Fame on the veteran ballot. He is only the third indoor player to receive the honor.

Former U.S. national team coach Lothar Osiander was elected to the Hall of Fame on the builder ballot. Osiander coached the senior national team in 1986-88 and the Under-23 team in 1988-92. He also had stints as head coach of the then-San Jose Clash and the LA Galaxy.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Finland's block on Russian athletes could affect NHL's return
stories.summary: The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes from entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in the future, the league told The Associated Press.
stories.body:
The NHL will consider Finland's plans to prevent Russian athletes from entering the country when deciding whether to stage more regular-season games there in the future, the league told The Associated Press.

Finland and Norway both announced plans to refuse entry to Russian athletes Thursday, the same day as the Carolina Hurricanes defeated the Seattle Kraken 4-1 in the first of two NHL regular-season games in the Finnish capital, Helsinki.

The Finnish restrictions take effect Monday, after the NHL games, and follow a backlash to Russia being reinstated in the hockey world championships, which is not an NHL event.

"We are aware of the government's position, and we'll have to take that into account," the league said Friday when asked if the new restrictions would be an obstacle to future games in Finland.

The Finnish foreign ministry's statement outlining the restrictions did not distinguish between Russian athletes on national teams, those competing as neutral athletes or those on club teams in sports like hockey or soccer.

The ministry said Thursday that Russians would be allowed to work in Finland only on "tasks that are essential to Finland's national interests." It added that Russia "uses sports as a propaganda tool."

The NHL has played regular-season games in Finland as part of its Global Series in 2022 and 2024. No future games have yet been announced.

As of the opening day of the 2026-27 season in September, there were 53 Russians on NHL rosters, making up 7.3% of the league. That was the fourth-largest contingent of players from any country.

Russian wing Andrei Svechnikov had an assist for the Hurricanes in Thursday's win. Pyotr Kochetkov was Carolina's backup goaltender. The Hurricanes and Kraken play again in Finland on Saturday.

The government decisions Thursday followed a backlash in Finland to Russia being reinstated for the ice hockey world championships, but its effects could mostly be felt in other sports. The International Skating Union warned of a "possible consequential impact" on its figure skating world championships in Finland in March.

Public broadcaster ERR reported Friday that Estonia had written to the International Ski and Snowboard Federation that athletes from Russia and its ally Belarus would not be allowed to enter the country. Estonia hosts the world junior championships in Nordic skiing in January.

stories.headline: Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad to continue at Racing Bulls for 2027
stories.summary: Liam Lawson will stay in Formula 1 alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad at Racing Bulls in 2027, ending weeks of speculation about the New Zealander's future.
stories.body:
Liam Lawson will stay in Formula 1 alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad at Racing Bulls in 2027, ending weeks of speculation about the New Zealander's future.

Lawson's place at the team had been under scrutiny in recent weeks, with Red Bull's Bulgarian junior Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings.

Racing Bulls ended any doubt on Thursday, confirming Lawson and Lindblad will continue together for another year.

Lawson has been one of the year's standout performers, sitting ninth with 89 points, a run of form which continued with a strong showing at last weekend's São Paulo Grand Prix, where he started third and finished seventh. Rookie teammate Lindblad is 11th with 38.

Racing Bulls is fighting for fifth in the constructors' championship.

- Qatar, Abu Dhabi races set to go ahead as F1 rules out Imola backup plan for finale

- Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border, urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in'

Team boss Alan Permane, who last week signed a deal to stay in his role until 2029, said Lawson and Lindblad is the strongest lineup the team could ask for.

"We're delighted to be continuing with Liam and Arvid for 2027," Permane said. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing. I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition.

"Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027."

Red Bull has confirmed Tsolov as reserve driver for Red Bull and Racing Bulls in 2027. The 19-year-old currently competes in Formula 2 for Campos Racing and is second in the title standings with two races remaining.

The team are promising an "extensive" programme of free practice sessions and Testing of Previous Car running as allowed under the F1 rulebook.

Tsolov said: "I'm incredibly happy and grateful to Red Bull for giving me this opportunity. Since joining the Junior Team, I've received amazing support and have developed so much, both as a driver and as a person. My career has progressed incredibly quickly, and I owe a lot to everyone who has believed in me and helped me get to this point.

"My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver. Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting. I'm confident that with the Team's support and experience, I'll have the best possible preparation to make sure I'm fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes."

stories.summary: The 2026 AFL draft is rapidly approaching, so here's your guide for what to know, including key dates and times, players to know, academy-linked names, and every club's pick.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL Draft is fast approaching. Marvel Stadium will once more play host to the first round at 7:00pm AEDT on November 19, with the draft recommencing for the second round onwards on November 20.

Key dates and times
Where: Marvel Stadium

How to watch: Fox Footy

First round: Thursday, November 19, 7pm AEDT

Second round onwards: Friday, November 20, 7pm AEDT

Preseason and rookie draft: Monday, November 23, 3pm AEDT

Each club's picks

*As at Nov. 11
Adelaide: 15, 32, 35, 43, 54

Brisbane: 21, 27, 28, 45

Carlton: 13, 18, 31, 50, 59, 67, 73

Collingwood: 11, 30, 63, 64, 65
